context: A police officer briefs a uni reporter about an investigation procedure
purpose: Teach: 主任/取り付け/採択/円滑/送付/法務省/官庁/査定

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 本件の経過、まず関係資料を法務省に送付した段階です。
lines.en: The status on this case is that we've just sent the relevant materials to the Justice Ministry.
lines.style: Professional and measured. Even pace, no hurry. Direct eye contact. The tone of someone who has given this briefing before and will give it again.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 査定の結果は、いつ頃出るんでしょうか。
lines.en: When do you expect the evaluation results to come back?
lines.style: Respectful but steady. Pen poised. No hesitation in the question — genuine curiosity from someone taking notes, not nervousness.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 官庁の事務がいま立て込んでいて、採択まで一ヶ月程度かかりそうです。
lines.en: The ministry's workload is heavy at the moment, so it'll likely take about a month before we see a decision.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, almost apologetic in tone but not in manner. A slight pause before the estimate, as if checking his memory. No embellishment.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 担当主任の方からは、追加情報はありそうですか。
lines.en: Is the chief manager in charge likely to have any additional information for you?
lines.style: Lean forward slightly. Practical question from someone who knows what will help his reporting. Clear, purposeful.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 明日の打合せで、円滑な情報共有を取り付けます。
lines.en: We'll work to secure a smooth flow of information at tomorrow's meeting.
lines.style: Steady commitment. A small nod of assurance. Professional but warm — not stiff. This is what he does: follow through.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。記事用にメモさせていただきます。
lines.en: Thank you. I'll make sure to note that down for the article.
lines.style: Genuine gratitude, not performative. A small bow of thanks. Settling back with notepad in hand, ready to move on. Respectful close.
